Plot Gauge

Source: R/fct_plots.R
plot_gauge.Rd

Plots the last reading of one sensor as a gauge, with the ideal range in green and a short note on what the gas and particle sensors measure. The ideal ranges of PM2.5 and PM10 are the 24-hour guidelines of the WHO (2021); PM1, which has none, gets that of PM2.5. The gas and proximity sensors have no fixed range, so their gauge is scaled to all the readings of data: it spans the lowest to the highest reading, widened by one standard deviation, the green band is the mean plus or minus one standard deviation, and the delta is the difference from the mean.

Usage

plot_gauge(data, variable = "Temperature")

Arguments

data

data frame from get_data(); the gauge shows its last reading

variable

one of "Temperature" "Humidity" "Pressure" "Lux" "Proximity" "NH3" "Reducing" "Oxidising" "PM1" "PM2.5" "PM10"

Value

A plotly object.

Examples

prometheus_url <- c(
  "http://pip1.crabdance.com:1507/api/v1/query_range",
  "http://pip1.crabdance.com:1505/api/v1/query_range"
)
filtered_df <- get_data(urlq = prometheus_url[1])
plot_gauge(data = filtered_df, variable = "Temperature")


plot_gauge(data = filtered_df, variable = "Humidity")


plot_gauge(data = filtered_df, variable = "PM2.5")
